articleTitle: Three Different Designs of Integrated Gate Drivers in 650-V e-Mode GaN Power IC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper presents the main characteristics of three different gate drivers monolithically integrated and realized in 650-V GaN-on-Si p-GaN Schottky gate technology. It compares the proposed circuits with state-of-the-art solutions and explains the tradeoff between propagation delay and gate driver current consumption. One of the proposed gate drivers can switch a 650-V 100 mΩ power transistor in less than 3 ns of fall time with a static power consumption of 1.1 mA. Another proposed gate driver uses a simplified approach to obtain similar performance. A third one achieves almost similar performance while requiring only one power supply rail operating in bootstrap topology. High-voltage and high-frequency measurements are presented for both zero voltage switching (ZVS) and hard switching conditions.

articleTitle: Contributions to Designing Undervoltage Lockout Circuits in p-GaN Gate Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper presents the main characteristics of four different UVLO (Undervoltage Lockout) circuits for monolithic integration in 650-V GaN-on-Si Schottky p-gate technology. The dispersion of the threshold values is measured and correlated with corner analysis and Monte Carlo simulation to analyze process variation. The objective is to achieve a design with low threshold value dispersion for mass production in an emerging GaN technology that exhibits significant variation in transistor threshold values and saturation current.

articleTitle: A 200V Monolithic GaN Half-Bridge with Active Gate Driver Including a Fast dv/dt Feedback Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN) transistors high switching speed enables lower switching losses compared to silicon transistors. However, their high switching speed can also cause electromagnetic disturbances (EMI), thus requiring new methods to mitigate the tradeoff between switching losses and EMI. This work presents a monolithic GaN Half-Bridge power stage using an on-chip Active Gate Driver (AGD) including a very fast dv/dt feedback loop to control the turn-on speed of the power transistor on a GaN-on-SOI technology. This feedback loop control method can achieve a 45% reduction of the dv/dt with a smaller impact on the commutation energy E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf> than a classical method using only either the gate resistor or the gate width of the driving transistor as a control parameter. Finally, a 2.5 × 5mm² prototype is developed using the IMEC GaN-on-SOI technology.

articleTitle: Sputtering Grown Wide Band Gap AlN Thin Films for High Power Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper reports on the characterization of optical and electrical properties of aluminum nitride (AlN) thin films, achieved by varying the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{2}/Ar$</tex> gas ratio during the sputtering process. Our findings reveal that AlN thin films can attain superior optical transmission in the visible spectrum compared to glass substrates, particularly at an optimal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{2}/Ar$</tex> ratio. Additionally, we observed that the dielectric strength and breakdown voltage of the films improve as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{2}/Ar$</tex> ratio decreases, reaching a dielectric strength of approximately 4.5× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> V/mm under optimized conditions. The study also demonstrates an increase in capacitance with higher applied DC voltage, attributed to the piezoelectric properties of AlN. These results highlight the potential of AlN thin films for applications in dielectric layers for power capacitors and gate materials in thin-film transistors.

articleTitle: Scaling Down Megawatt-Level SSTs: Prototype Design and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Testing megawatt-level electric vehicle (EV) fast charging stations is challenging due to the high costs, the need for high voltage sources, and high-power loads. This study introduces a scaled-down prototype of a MW-level solid-state transformer (SST)-based EV fast charger focusing on low-cost and modular design principles. Each sub-module (SM) integrates active front-end (AFE) and dual active bridge (DAB) stages within a compact structure, ensuring scalability and flexibility. Operating in a three-phase configuration, the prototype demonstrates 1.8 kW per unit, which is shared on 9 SMs per phase, representing 1 MW in total capacity. The paper emphasizes the significance of scaled-down prototypes in verification of the overall system performance and control algorithms, showcasing their pivotal role in refining design methodologies and advancing SST technology. Through systematic verification of the overall system and distributed control, this research highlights the potential of scaled-down SST prototypes to drive innovation in power electronic applications, promising enhanced efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness in future deployments.

articleTitle: Self-Heating and Hotspots in GaN HEMTs with Conventional and T-Shape Gates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Self-heating effects and hotspots due to an electric field and a field-induced trap generation are studied in two conventional 1 µm gate length GaN HEMTs with widths of 50 µm and 100 µm, and two Tshaped 250 nm gate length GaN HEMTs with the same gate widths. The study of self-heating and hotspots in the access region between the gate and the drain uses a combination of experiments and TCAD simulations. The simulations are calibrated against experimental I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> characteristics at high and low drain voltages assuming a self-heating and a generation of deep carbon traps between the gate and the drain induced by a high electric field. We demonstrate that carbon traps act as deep or shallow traps depending on the GaN HEMT gate architecture and show that the T-gate HEMT architecture exhibits only shallow traps thanks to a more uniform electric field distribution in the drain region.

articleTitle: Steady-State Analysis of Standalone Vertical Silicon & SiC NPN BJTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: SiC BJTs have enabled a significant increase in the DC current gain compared with their Silicon counterparts. The absence of the gate oxide, as a known reliability concern in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>iC MOSFETs, has enabled high-gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>iC BJTs to find popularity in certain applications. This paper has investigated the temperature-dependance of vertical high voltage NPN Silicon and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>iC BJTs and sheds light on the similarities and differences in static analysis. Measurements are conducted on key electrical properties: Transfer characteristics, Base-Emitter leakage Cur-rent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{R(BE)})$</tex>, Collector-Emitter on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{R}_{on})$</tex>, DC common-Emitter current gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\beta)$</tex> and Output (I-V) characteristics.

articleTitle: The Impact of Varying the High-Temperature Post-Deposition Anneal Time or Temperature Ramp Rates on ALD-SiO2/4H-SiC Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: A Post-deposition annealing (PDA) study on atomic layer deposited (ALD)-SiO2/4H-SiC Metal-oxide semiconductor capacitors (MOSCAPs) is presented in this paper. This paper reports that varying the annealing time in conventional PDA (in Nitrous oxide or forming gas) and in forming gas rapid thermal annealing (RTA) PDA does not affect the electrical parameters of the MOS interface. Varying the annealing temperature for forming gas quartz PDA does not affect the electrical parameters either. Flatband voltage, hysteresis, and frequency dispersion of the MOS interface individually all had a positive correlation against the temperature ramp rate, while the annealing time and temperature were kept constant. This result subsequently led to a thermal budget investigation of all PDAs, revealing that thermal budget affects the flatband voltage and hysteresis of the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/4H-SiC MOS interface.

articleTitle: On the Design and Effectiveness of Isolation Trenches to Suppress Substrate Coupling in Power Integrated Circuits in GaN-on-Si Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: We present electromagnetic (EM) investigation of isolation trenches of feasible designs and their effectiveness to suppress substrate coupling in power integrated circuits (ICs) in GaN-on-Si technology. The S-parameter results reveal that the air-filled or SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-filled design (etching the GaN buffer layer) can improve the signal isolation by about 8 dB (from -59 dB to -67 dB in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{21}\vert$</tex> at 20 MHz) for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$700-\mu m$</tex> lateral separation distance, with only very slight improvement (0.6 dB) for a grounded aluminum-filled trench. Using a wider trench has almost no help in improving the signal isolation indicated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{21}\vert$</tex>. The lateral position of the trench does not impact the signal isolation either. The electric field profiles obtained from EM simulations unveil the substrate coupling through the p-type Si substrate when using an isolation trench in the GaN buffer layer. These results can provide helpful guidelines for the monolithic integration of power electronic devices and circuits in GaN-on-Si technology.

articleTitle: Experimental Results on Electrical Characteristics of 2DEG Resistors in GaN-on-Si Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: We report electrical characteristics of two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) resistors for power integrated circuits (ICs) in GaN-on-Si technology. The 2DEG resistors essentially stem from depletion-mode AlGaN/GaN metal-insulator semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (MIS-HEMTs) with the gate terminal configured open-circuit. From the on-wafer measurements of devices with various layout sizes, the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics display linear behaviour for a voltage drop within ≈ 2 V. Steady DC resistance of the 2DEG resistors ranges from 35 Ωto almost 1 kΩ, with a sheet resistance of about 400 Ω/square. However, when the 2-terminal voltage increases beyond about 3 V, the 2DEG resistors no longer follow Ohm's law: the current starts to level off steadily because of the expected velocity saturation of electrons in GaN. At about 10 V for our fabricated devices, the 2DEG resistance increases non-linearly to about nearly doubled. These characteristics bring implications that 2DEG resistors are useful for small voltage but need proper device modelling for use in especially high-voltage circuits.

articleTitle: Impact of Temperature on Dynamics and Reliability of High-Voltage Silicon & 4H-SiC Bipolar Junction Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper analyses the impact of high temperature on the dynamic characteristics and performance of the highest voltage bipolar junction transistors available commercially: an 800 V, 20 A Fairchild Silicon BJT and a 1.7 kV, 15 A GeneSiC 4H-SiC BJT, under conditions of high injection levels, unclamped inductive switching, and short circuit at case temperatures of at least 150°C. The high temperature investigations are conducted through measurements at a range of base resistance and collector currents. Clamped inductive switching tests have been performed at 800 V with a maximum collector current of 14 A, varying the switching rates. In the unclamped inductive switching and short circuit tests, the stress level is increased by either raising the DC-link voltage or extending the pulse length until device failure. According to the dynamic transient results, 4H-SiC BJTs outperform their Silicon counterparts, exhibiting a DC current gain at least ten times higher than that of Silicon and faster switching performance without delay in transitions. The withstand energy density in reliability tests are also higher in SiC thanks to significantly smaller die size.

articleTitle: Soft-Switched SiC Based DC-DC Converter with Low-Loss Modulation in DC-AC Inverter for Highly Efficient EV/HEV Powertrains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper introduces a Silicon Carbide (SiC) based powertrain for Electric/Hybrid Electric Vehicles (EV/HEV) featuring a cascaded topology. The design comprises a DC-DC stage with a three-phase interleaved boost converter (IBC) employing SiC MOSFETs switching at 250 kHz, followed by a DC-ACstage utilizing a three-phase inverter. The integration of soft switching in the DC-DC stage and the implementation of a low-loss PWM method i.e., 240°-Clamped Pulse Width Modulation (240CPWM) in the DC-AC stage aim to significantly enhance powertrain's efficiency. Thermal modeling and simulation results at 10 kW validate the efficacy of the proposed topology in achieving high efficiency in EV/HEV powertrains. The combined efficiency of DC-DC stage and DC-AC stage with the proposed topology is as high as 98% as opposed to 95% in conventional topology at 10 kW.

articleTitle: A Temperature-Correlated Simulink Model of Single-Stage Thermoelectric Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Single-stage thermoelectric modules have a wide range of applications in energy recovery, energy management, and temperature regulation. The simulation model of the thermoelectric modules is very important for analyzing the thermoelectric conversion process. In this paper, a temperature-correlated (TC) Simulink model is proposed for single-stage thermoelectric modules. Firstly, the expressions of the internal resistance and the Seebeck coefficient of the single-stage thermoelectric module are improved by considering the temperature characteristics, and further verified by comparing the obtained curves of the internal resistance, optimal voltage and optimal power of the single-stage thermoelectric module with the experimental results provided in the module's datasheet. Secondly, a Simulink package with a controlled voltage source is established for this improve single-stage thermoelectric module, It can be directly used in the following energy harvest boost converter, next, this Simulink model is used and verified in the boost converter using the perturb and observe (P&O) and Increment Conductance (IC) maximum power point tracking algorithm. Therefore, this paper provides an effective TC Simulink model of the single-stage thermoelectric modules, which can be used not only for research on the material characteristic of the thermoelectric modules, but also for the research on the following energy harvest circuits.

articleTitle: Neutron Radiation-Induced Failure Rate of 650 V Lateral GaN Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Power semiconductors made from Gallium Nitride hold great potential for demanding applications for example in aircraft power electronic systems. Here, the design needs to consider device failure due to cosmic ray, where neutrons are the most critical particles. In contrast to Silicon and Silicon Carbide devices, failure data of Gallium Nitride transistors are not widely available. In this paper, the failure rate of Gallium Nitride transistors with a rated voltage of 650 V was determined by accelerated neutron irradiation and compared to Silicon Carbide devices. For Gallium Nitride, failures could only be observed at voltages above the rated voltage and close to the breakdown voltage, demonstrating the great potential of Gallium Nitride devices, considering the current device technologies.

articleTitle: Integrating Wide Bandgap Semiconductor Technologies into Emerging Mobile Energy Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Future energy systems are gradually more susceptible to disruptions due to reduced network redundancy. It is urgent to develop additional flexible resources to improve energy network resilience. Mobile energy supply systems (MOES), typically denoted as truck-mounted generators, can play an important role due to its spatial-temporal flexibility compared with their stationary counterparts. This paper assesses the possibility of integrating advanced wide bandgap (WBG) technologies into emerging mobile energy supply systems. The research firstly starts with the typical configuration and functionality analysis of MOES, investigating potential energy solutions, and then proposes several key performance indicators in relation to MOES. Subsequently, the potential of WBG technologies in different configurations of MOES is investigated. The research demonstrates the promising potential of combing WBG with MOES to enhance its functionality in supporting the operation of future energy systems.

articleTitle: A Simplified Method for SiC Mosfet Spice Models Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: With advances in electric vehicle (EV) technology, the use of SiC MOSFETs for power converters has increased. To facilitate converter design, accurate and robust SPICE models for MOSFET devices are essential. Although existing solutions, including the modified Enz-Krummenacher Vittoz (EKV) model, exist, they often lack detailed specifications of model parameters. This study provides detailed insights into the parameters of the Wolfspeed C2M0040120D model, highlighting the dominance of the threshold voltage, drift resistance and transconductance fitting curves. By adjusting these curves, the manufacturer's model accuracy in the on-state was improved from 69% to 50%, with a maximum mismatch with the datasheet for the first EKV model variant (EKV model v1). To further improve the results, the paper proposed an optimization algorithm that defines the best set of fitting parameters based on the total error cost function to find a second EKV model variant (EKV model v2). The new model showed a better match, reducing the maximum static mismatch to 22%. The double-pulse test conducted on the EKV model v2 shows improved matching in switching, which was verified by experimental results and faster simulation.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance Improvement Potential of Top and Bottom-Cooled Power-SOIC Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This study evaluates the thermal performance of power-SOIC packaged devices that find applications in wide-bandgap technology, and which can be offered to be implemented on a top- or bottom-cooled solution. The potential of improving the package technology by utilizing advanced substrates such as Silicon Nitride (Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) is assessed, which provides additional benefits for wide-bandgap devices, including voltage isolation. The study simulates and validates the proposed solution by packaging the devices and implementing the improvements recommended. Experimental validation is conducted through full electrothermal characterization to obtain temperature profiles, structure functions, thermal resistances, and estimated chip temperatures using temperature sensitive electric parameters (TSEP). The results show potential improvements of approximately 14% in thermal performance.

articleTitle: Double-Voltage Short-Circuit Protection Circuit for SiC MOSFETs with Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper presents a double-voltage short-circuit protection circuit for SiC MOSFETs with temperature compensation, where the gate voltage reference threshold value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{ref1}(T))$</tex> is relative to the switching-on Miller platform voltage and is temperature-dependent, and the blanking time for HSF is determined by the time of the gate voltage rise to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}(T)$</tex> and is dynamically self-adaptive with the junction temperature to assure the short-circuit protection circuit trigger fast. This method can effectively reduce the peak value of overcurrent and protect the device quickly from short-circuit destruction. In double pulse tests, With the temperature-dependent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}(T)$</tex>, HSF detection time is 80 ns at room temperature and 62 ns at 120 °C. HSF detecting time is reduced by 25 % compared to the fixed Vref1. The drain current at HSF detecting trigger point is 38.6 A, 25.6 A, and 48.4 A, respectively and the overcurrent peak value after the HSF detection trigger point is 88.9 A, 93.1 A, and 106.6 A, respectively, for the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}(25\ {}^{\circ} C), V_{ref1}(120\ {}^{\circ} C)$</tex> and the fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}$</tex> for 120 °C. The drain current at HSF detecting trigger point and the overcurrent peak value are reduced by 47 % and 12.71 % respectively for the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}$</tex> (120°C) and the fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{ref1}$</tex> for 120°C. For FUL detecting delay time, it is 69 ns for all junction temperatures. The proposed short-circuit protection method can quickly detect the HSF error, suppress the overcurrent at high junction temperatures, and improve the reliability of SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Understanding Inter-Chip Oscillations in Paralleled SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This study analyzes self-excited inter-chip oscillations in paralleled SiC MOSFETs. Initial measurements and simulations demonstrating these oscillations are presented. A novel stability analysis approach based on Modified Nodal Analysis (MNA) is then proposed, offering significantly greater speed and flexibility compared to conventional methods. This method allows for the detailed investigation of asymmetric layout and chip parameters. Simulation and measurement results are subsequently provided to demonstrate the dependence of oscillation amplitude on bias conditions, including DC-link voltage, load current, and switching speed.

articleTitle: On-Wafer RON Degradation Analysis of 100 V p-GaN HEMTs Emulating Low- and High-Side Operation in Half Bridge Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: We developed a custom setup for the on-wafer dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> evaluation of 100 V p-GaN HEMTs emulating low- (LS) and high-side (HS) operation in integrated half-bridge circuits. We found that RON degradation is more pronounced in HS configuration compared to the LS one, while similar time constants and activation energies were extracted. This suggests that the underlying physical mechanism is the same in both cases, i.e., hole emission from C-related acceptors in the GaN buffer. Numerical device simulations were carried out to explain the different degree of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> degradation in LS and HS operation.

articleTitle: A Short Circuit Testing and Ruggedness Study of Latest SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: SiC power semiconductors offer high switching speed and high breakdown voltage which allows for increased system-level power density. Therefore, the use of SiC power semiconductors in the automotive and aerospace markets is increasing. However, the reliability of SiC devices is a key parameter responsible for the successful deployment in EV applications. SiC MOSFETs face various challenges when employed in power electronic converters, one of these challenges is the behaviour and protection during a short circuit event within a SiC power converter. An accurate desaturation methodology can be employed when short circuit withstand time (SCWT) and critical energy are known. This paper investigates the behaviour of the latest generation SiC TO-247 devices from two leading manufacturers in the SiC device market under short circuit type I conditions. The detailed design and parameter selection for the short circuit type I test are discussed along with presenting experimental results.

articleTitle: An Experimental Performance Comparison of GaN and Silicon Based FETs in an Emergency LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Gallium Nitride (G<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>N) High-Electron-Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) are currently prominent in the power electronics literature due to the increasing viability of use across all industries. However, there are still gaps in the GaN related literature due to the vast coverage of power electronics. One such gap is in understanding the efficiency benefit of GaN devices compared to Silicon in an Emergency LED Driver application. In addition, the on resistance and parasitic capacitances of the GaN device play important roles in selecting the optimal device for the converter. This paper presents experimental results of a direct swap of various Schottky Gate E Mode GaN devices compared to an NMOS Silicon device for a Low Power, Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS), Boundary Conduction Mode (BCM) Emergency LED driver converter, addressing the gap in literature. A 20 percent efficiency boost over silicon is observed in the megahertz region, using a Schottky diode antiparallel to the FET.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Characteristics of Schottky-Type and Ohmic-Type p-GaN Gate GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: P-GaN gate GaN HEMTs can be categorized into Schottky-type and ohmic-type regarding the gate contact, resulting in different behaviors of the transistors. This paper presents a comparative study of both types based on experimental results. Extensive characterizations are conducted including leakage current, intrinsic capacitances, output characteristics, and the threshold voltage instability. The impact of various parameters on the transistor characteristics is studied under both static and dynamic measurement conditions. The investigation is application-oriented, aiming to enhance understanding and facilitate the application of p-GaN gate GaN transistors.

Index Terms: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated Two-Stage GaN Gate Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This work presents the design, characterization, and optimization of a monolithically integrated two-stage GaN gate driver. The individually combinable stages provide a high degree of flexibility and can realize different driver topologies. The driver is also optionally manufactured with pad over active layout. Two driver supply concepts can be implemented and evaluated. Dynamic and static on-wafer measurements are shown. Optimization of the driver is performed for various design goals such as power consumption, rise/fall time and delay time. Finally, the results are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Design of a 650V 400A Half-Bridge GaN Power Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: In order to take full advantage of the high switching speeds of gallium nitride (GaN) devices in high-power-density applications, a novel approach to reducing power loop stray inductance by reducing and equalising the current loops of paralleled devices, is presented in this paper. The design of a unique substrate layout, that serves to evenly distribute current to the paralleled devices is described in detail, and then verified through simulation using ANSYS Q3D. The simulation results are then compared with measurements of the physical device, to determine the effectiveness and feasibility of the design.

articleTitle: A Comparative Evaluation of the Surge Current Robustness of Modern Power Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Inverter surge current capability has become increasingly more important in today's grid infrastructure as synchronous generation is being replaced by inverter-based resources. Grid strength challenges such as limited voltage support and control instabilities have risen due to the surge current boundaries imposed by the thermal limitations of the conventional semiconductors used in inverters. The goal of this paper is to investigate and compare the surge current robustness of various discrete power transistor technologies, such that the capabilities of commercial inverters can be pushed further to facilitate a seamless transition to increased integration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Three-Phase SiC-Based Voltage/Current-Source Inverter Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: Variable speed drives (VSDs) operating from a common dc bus enable significant energy savings in variable-load centrifugal systems like pumps and compressors. Ideally, VSDs should provide smooth sinusoidal motor voltages to ensure compatibility with standard motors. Thus, voltage-source inverters (VSIs) equipped with an output filter or current-source inverters (CSIs) are candidate topologies. Using multi-objective Pareto optimization, this paper provides a comprehensive comparative evaluation of VSI and CSI topology and modulation variants, which employ 1200 V and/or 900 V SiC power transistors and drive a 400 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> (line-to-line rms), 7.5 kW high-speed permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) with a high nominal output frequency of up to 2 kHz from a 750 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> dc bus. The results indicate comparable performance of VSI and CSI topologies in terms of efficiency (weighted according to the NEMA power index load profile) and power density, yet the CSI designs require larger total chip areas at least until 900 V monolithic bidirectional power transistors become available. Advantageously, the CSI's de-side voltage-to-current conversion stage (dc-dc buck converter) can be realized with two interleaved phases that each operate in a triangular-current mode (TCM) and hence with soft-switching, while the dc-link current still shows a low ripple only; this approach clearly outperforms all other considered variants.

articleTitle: Wide Bandgap Power Electronic Devices for Constraint Management in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: This paper investigates the value of wide bandgap (WBG) technology in enhancing constraint management in distribution networks. The paper firstly provides a review of existing constraint management technologies. The advantages of power electronic technology over other technologies are highlighted, while the challenges of power electronics that normally use silicon (Si) materials are discussed. To address these challenges, this paper introduces WBG semiconductor technology as an innovative solution. The benefits of WBG power electronics for network constraint management including reduced cost, high energy conversion efficiency and high applicability are then identified. Based on these benefits, their promising applications in constraint management of distribution networks are also summarized.

articleTitle: Enhancing High-Power-Density Converter Design: A Data-Driven Analysis of MOSFET and Heatsink Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Wide Bandgap Power Devices and Applications in Europe (WiPDA Europe)
abstract: MOSFETs are commonly used switching devices in high-power-density converters thanks to their fast-switching frequency. However, their on-state resistance and high switching frequency result in undesirable heat dissipation, which leads to thermal management challenges. To prevent device overheating, failure, and safety hazards, heatsinks for cooling are essential. This study aims to address the optimal combined selection of MOSFETs and heatsinks for designing high-power-density converters by analyzing extensive MOSFET and heatsink data from electronics distributors and utilizing data imputation to handle missing data related to MOSFET and heatsink specifications. This paper establishes a comprehensive data-driven model, supported by data imputation, that estimates the converters' power dissipation and temperature of MOSFETs and heatsinks based on design parameters including voltage levels, current levels, costs, and volumes. Predicting power dissipation and junction temperature under varying design parameters aids engineers in making suitable choices during the practical design process.
